# `kernel/VRAMTracker.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/VRAMTracker.js`

VRAMTracker.js — per-app GPU memory budget tracking. WebGPU does not expose actual VRAM usage. We track *requested* allocations: Surfaces  — estimated from canvas dimensions × bytes-per-pixel Buffers   — exact size passed to createBuffer (when routed via syscalls) Textures  — estimated from width × height × format bytes-per-pixel Admission is checked before allocations. Canvas surfaces receive a small, bounded reserve so buffer/texture workloads cannot consume the final UI capacity and make an app impossible to close or recover. Phase 5+ upgrade path: hook device.createBuffer/createTexture via a GPUDevice proxy to track all allocations, not just syscall-routed ones.

## Functions

### `createGpuMountAllocationAccounting(tracker, appId)`

Kernel-only accounting seam, not an owner/Realm authority factory. Unsupported tracker implementations return null, never fabricated zero measurements. The broker binds the powerless scope token to its genuine mount lease. Forgotten accounting stays unavailable even if that app ID is reused.

### `createGpuSurfaceAllocationAccounting(tracker, appId, panelId)`

Private attribution over the existing numeric surface-reservation ledger. A scope describes one original manager surface, not an app/mount authority. Displacement or forgetting loses attribution permanently; neither is zero.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
